quote_original: I thought I had said it.
context_before: Now that is really what I meant.
context_after: That I may not be misunderstood, that is my principle. You and I can contemplate an ideal, and become it by falling in love with it.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: If this is true, to whom would I go?
context_before: But to tell me that I am the cause of all that happens to me that I am forever molding my world in harmony with my inner nature, that is more than man is willing to accept.
context_after: If these are the words of eternal life, I must return to them, even though they seem so difficult to digest.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Son is a concept, an idea.
context_before: All that thou gavest me I have kept in thy name, and none have I lost save the son of perdition. The son of perdition means simply the belief in loss.
context_after: Perdido is loss. I have only truly lost the concept of loss, for nothing can be lost.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Therefore you cannot turn to anyone outside of self.
context_before: Any enlargement of our concept of Self involves a somewhat painful parting with strongly rooted hereditary conceptions. The ligaments are strong that hold us in the womb of conventional limitations. All that you formerly believed, you no longer believe. You know now that there is no power outside of your own consciousness.
context_after: You have no ears for the suggestion that something else has power in it. You know the only reality is God, and God is your own consciousness. There is
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self

quote_original: Then I become the blessed, I become Isaac.
context_before: I quietly appropriate that which no man can give me, no woman can give me. I dare to assume that I am God. This must be of faith, this must be of promise.
context_after: As I begin to do the things that only this presence could do, I know that I am born out of the limitations of Ishmael, and I have become heir to the k
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Then I seemed to be walking in the night.
context_before: exaltation of those who had been conquerors in a conflict with death, were singing, “He is risen -He is risen,” and intuitively I knew they meant me.
context_after: I soon came upon a scene that might have been the ancient Pool of Bethesda for in this place lay a great multitude of impotent folk — blind, halt, withered -waiting not for the moving of the water as of tradition, but waiting for me.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Toy with the idea of perfection.
context_before: s elongated, yet he is the same man. Or he looks into another mirror and he is all big and fat. These things are seen today because man is what he is.
context_after: Ask no man to help you, but let the prayer of the 17th chapter of the Gospel of St. John be your prayer. Appropriate the state that was yours before the world was.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: For example, suppose I wanted now to be elsewhere.
context_before: Desire is the mainspring of all action. Now what do I want? I must define my objective.
context_after: This very moment I really desire to be elsewhere. I need not go through the door, I need not sit down. I need do nothing but stand just where I am and with my eyes closed, assume that I am actually standing where I desire to be. Then I remain in this state until it has the feeling of reality. Were I now elsewhere I could not see the world as I now see it from here. The world changes in its relationship to me as I change my position in space.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: You would embrace him, wouldn’t you?
context_before: Suppose you were now to meet a friend that you have not seen for a year and he is a friend of whom you are very fond. What would you do?
context_after: Or you would put your hand upon him.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Restrict the action to just that.
context_before: In your imagination bring him close enough to put your hand upon him and feel him to be solidly real.
context_after: You will be amazed at what happens. From then on things begin to move. Your dimensionally greater self will inspire, in all, the ideas and actions necessary to bring you into physical contact. It works that way.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: I have another way of praying.
context_before: when you will be free you can create it. I would not suggest that you do it lightly, because you will feel very, very sleepy and you may not want to.
context_after: In this case I always sit down and I find the most comfortable arm chair imaginable, or I lie flat on my back and relax completely. Make yourself comfortable. You must not be in any position where the body is distressed. Always put yourself into a position where you have the greatest ease. That is the first stage.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: That is all you need do.
context_before: What would I feel like, now, were I what I want to be? When I know what the feeling would be like I then close my eyes and lose myself in that single sensation and my dimensionally greater Self then builds a bridge of incident to lead me from this present moment to the fulfillment of my mood.
context_after: But people have a habit of slighting the importance of simple things.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

author: Neville Goddard
source_title: Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: You are Jesus of the story.
context_before: The story has nothing to do with a man riding on a little colt.
context_after: The colt is the mood you are going to assume. That is the living animal not yet ridden by you. What would the feeling be like were you to realize your desire? A new feeling, like a young Colt, is a very difficult thing to ride unless you ride him with a disciplined mind. If I do not remain faithful to the mood the young colt throws me off. Every time you become conscious that you are not faithful to this mood, you have been thrown from the colt.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Lesson 4 – No One To Change But Self (1968-01-01).

rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Do remain faithful to this instruction.
context_before: The test of a teacher, or a teaching, is to be found in the faithfulness of the taught. I am leaving here on Sunday night.
context_after: If you look for causes outside the consciousness of man, then I have not convinced you of the reality of consciousness.
